texts: doha on who we really are underneath everything?
Unborn, undying, older than the first breath, it was never made and cannot be unmade; sing the one who dwells within.
Standing at the hospital bed, I wondered what part of my father had not been touched by all the sickness and would go on.
Write a verse about the part of me that was never born and will never die, the watcher that stays the same through every age, every name, and every change that life brings.
the deathless soul
soul, never born
When my mother lost her memory I kept asking who she still was underneath, and I felt there was something that no illness could take away.
who am i really? doha pls
Compose a doha that tells us we are not our name, our job, or our story but the quiet, unborn awareness behind them all that has never aged and will never end.
Before the first cry and after the last sigh, one who watches stands, untouched by what comes and goes.
Give me a verse about the real self within every person, which no blow can cut and no sorrow can stain, which was never born and cannot die, and which only seems to suffer.
doha on the deathless self that never changes
After my accident I felt that the real me had never been hurt at all, as if it stood watching quietly from far away.
eternal, unborn, untouched
Names and shapes come and go, but the one who sees remains, unborn, unwounded, the same.
soul beyond skeleton, sun
The skeleton bleaches in the sun; the one who lived in it never aged, never left, never was.
doha about the soul being more than a skeleton and a sun-baked life
Visiting the museum I stared at an old skeleton in the sun-lit hall and felt very sure that whoever lived in it was not those bones.
Write a verse that tells how the skeleton lying in the sun was only a coat the soul once wore, and that the one who wore it has never been born and has never been lost.
Grandma folded the old cotton clothes and said the one who wore them is not in them; a snake had left its skin by the doorstep that same day.
doha on the soul changing clothes like a snake sheds skin, also cotton
cotton, snake, changeless one
Write a doha explaining that the real self is never harmed when the garment is changed, as a snake slips out of its skin or a person drops worn cotton, for the wearer is unborn and whole.
The cotton is plucked and the snake sheds its skin, and the unborn wearer walks on in a fresh garment.
crow, beggar, full self
u know the doha where the self isn't the crow's hunger or the beggar's want? want one like that
Compose a couplet that says the crow's hunger and the beggar's need belong to the passing life, not to the true self, which has no hunger, no want, and no lack of any kind.
A beggar on my street told me that his stomach was empty but that something inside him was entirely full and never needed anything, and a crow sat beside him.
The crow caws of hunger, the beggar of need, but the one within asks for nothing and lacks nothing.
crossroads, oil press, stillness
doha about the changeless self at a crossroads, oil press too
Write a doha about the true self that stays still at every crossroads of life, unmoved by the grinding of the oil press of days, watching everything and being ground by nothing.
At the crossroads the world is pressed like oil, yet the Self within is never pressed or spent.
Watching the crossroads full of people rushing to the oil press queue, I felt there was one in me that never rushes anywhere.
doha on the soul, pure like milk, hard as stone
Compose a verse on the deathless self that is as pure as milk and as unbreakable as stone, which neither fades with time nor spoils with use and cannot be stained by anything.
When my uncle was dying, I noticed the one who looked out of his eyes was as steady as stone and as clean as fresh milk, as if untouched.
milk, stone, undying self
Pure as milk, firm as stone, the Self within has no beginning and no end.
Write a doha for the cremation ground that says the pyre consumes only what was borrowed, and the one who lived within is unborn and cannot be touched by any blaze, smoke, or heat.
cremation ground, the unburnt one
Standing at the cremation ground I felt sure that the person we loved had not been burned at all, only the clothes of that person.
doha on what remains at the cremation ground
The pyre burns the form to nothing, but the one who dwelt there steps out unscorched.
Dew gathers and vanishes, sandalwood is cut and still sweet; the Self within stays whole through every change.
Write a doha about the inner Self that is like the scent of sandalwood, that stays sweet though it is ground to paste and never changes, and that is not lost like the dew when the day grows hot.
dew, sandalwood, pure self
My grandmother's body shrank like dew in the morning but her presence stayed fragrant as sandalwood, and I felt she was not leaving.
doha on the self being sandalwood and not dew
sandalwood, unchanging core
Write a verse about the soul being like sandalwood that gives its fragrance even to the axe that cuts it, whose true nature is never harmed, and whose real self is always sweet.
Cut the sandalwood, still it breathes its scent; harm the shell, still the Self is whole.
A carpenter once cut sandalwood in front of me and told me the fragrance was still the same in every sliver, which made me think of how the soul stays whole.
doha about the soul as sandalwood please
The crow's cry fades across the field, but the silent one who hears it was never born and will never fade.
crow, silent self
Compose a verse on how the crow shouts and flaps about while the Self watches in silence, never moved by noise, never needing to be heard, and abiding in a stillness older than any sound.
the crow is loud but the self is silent, need a doha
Sitting on the roof at dawn while a crow screamed, I realized that whoever noticed the sound was quieter than the sound.
nameless essence
No name could hold it, no shape could hide it; it is what remains when everything has been taken away.
what's left of me when everything is gone? doha
Give me a doha on the nameless essence of a person, the one that remains when title, age, and story are stripped, which cannot be measured, aged, wounded, or finished, and is simply what I am.
After I lost my job, my place in the world, and my reputation all in one year, I discovered someone in me who was still entirely fine.
cuckoo, net, free self
The old woman held her illness like a cuckoo in a net, yet her face shone as if the one inside it was perfectly free.
The cuckoo sings in the net, and the net holds only the song's body; the singer within flies free.
a doha on the self and the cuckoo caught in the net
Write a doha about the cuckoo caught in the net that cannot hold the true bird inside it, for the Self within every living thing is boundless, unbound, and never truly captured.
Through all the scandals at my office, my friend somehow stayed untouched, a lotus in the mire, as if her real self stood apart from it all.
The lotus rises in mud and stays unspotted; the Self lives in the world and is never stained by it.
Write a doha for the deathless self which lives among all the muddy dealings of the world and remains unstained, like a lotus on which no drop ever clings.
doha: the soul is like a lotus, untouched
lotus, unstained self
The jeweller weighed my grandfather's ring on the scales and I thought about how nothing like that could weigh him, and a bee hummed on his window.
doha on the soul that scales can't weigh and bees can't reach
scales, bee, immeasurable self
The scales weigh everything but the weigher; the bee tastes every sweetness but the taster; so is the Self.
Write a verse that tells how no scales can weigh the soul and no bee can sip its true sweetness, for it is beyond measure, beyond price, and beyond all that can be counted or taken.
doha about the soul as the passenger and the body as the boat?
boat, passenger self
The boat may sink in the stream; the sitter steps to the shore, unwet, undimmed.
Write a doha about the Self as the passenger sitting in the boat of this life, who does not drown when the boat breaks, who steps ashore unharmed, and who was never the vessel in the first place.
When the old fishing boat finally sank at our harbour, my grandfather, who had sailed it for fifty years, just said the sailor is never lost with the boat.
tree, undying self
The tree is felled, but the life that was in it moves on, unborn and deathless.
Write a doha that says the tree grows and falls, but the life within it, like the Self within us, was never born with it and never dies with it, only moves on into another form.
doha about the soul being like the tree, the same forever
When the old tree behind our school was cut down, our teacher said that the part of it that mattered had not gone anywhere.
Gold may be melted and a leaf may fall, but the Self within has no melting point and no autumn.
I once watched a goldsmith melt old jewellery in his workshop and a leaf drift in, and I felt something in me that never goes through such changes.
gold, leaf, the unchanging
doha on gold and a leaf, about the soul never changing
Compose a verse about the deathless soul which is like gold that cannot be corroded and like a leaf that falls without harming the branch, for it was never born and has no end.
As a child I once asked my teacher who is it that looks through my eyes, and he smiled and said you are the one asking.
Give me a verse that answers the question of what I really am, saying I am neither young nor old, neither man nor woman, neither this name nor that, but the unborn witness within.
Not this, not that, not the one who is called by a name, but the quiet knower who was never begun.
what is the soul exactly? doha
witness, deathless, unborn
house, dweller within
Write a doha about the dweller who lives in the house of this life for a short while, who does not change when the walls crack, and who walks out calmly when the lease of the years is over.
doha about the soul and the house it lives in
After the storm broke our roof, my mother said that she was not this house, nor was the family she fed, but something quieter that nothing could take.
The house falls down, the dweller does not; how long was he a stranger there!
river, forehead mark, the Self
Compose a verse that says no river can wash the soul and no forehead mark can add to it, for it is unborn, perfect, and complete, and neither pilgrimage nor sign can make it more than it is.
The river flows on, the forehead mark fades by noon; the Self within was whole before either.
At the ghat, I saw a man dip into the river and put on his forehead mark, and I wondered what exactly he thought was being improved.
doha: the soul isn't changed by rivers or forehead marks
Write a doha on the same deathless Self living in the elephant and in the bee, equal in the mighty and in the minute, unchanged by size, strength, or the span of days each one lives.
The elephant is mighty, the bee is tiny, but the Self dwells equally in both, undying in the great and the small.
doha about the same soul in an elephant and a bee
elephant, bee, same soul
I watched an elephant and a bee in the garden and had a quiet feeling that the same unborn one looked out of both their eyes.
My friend's son was pronounced gone yet his mother insisted that something of him was still entirely unharmed, and I could not tell her she was wrong.
never dies, never born
Please compose a doha for the one who asks whether anything in a person truly survives, telling him that the self is neither born nor destroyed and that only its appearances come and go.
doha about the part of us that doesn't die
It was never born so it cannot die; it only appears and disappears like a guest passing through time.
prayer beads, inn, wayfarer
At the inn on my pilgrimage I counted my prayer beads and realised that the counter was neither the beads nor the inn nor the tiredness.
doha on prayer beads, an inn, and who I really am
Write a doha on the Self that is not the prayer beads nor the inn where it spent a night, the Self that was before both, that remains after both, and is never the thing it touches.
Prayer beads slip through the hand and the inn is left at dawn; the Self that is neither beads nor inn walks on.
The tortoise folds into its shell, and who can say what lives within; so the Self lives within and is not the shell.
tortoise, hidden Self

Write a verse on the tortoise that draws in its limbs and shows no sign of life, and on the Self within us that draws itself inward and is found unchanged, unborn, and undisturbed by the world outside.
doha about a tortoise and the true self
My grandmother, slow as a tortoise in her last year, kept insisting she was the same inside as she was at twenty.
doha on the self as what a touchstone can't change
touchstone, true self
Rub me on the touchstone of sorrow, and what shows is not me but the colour of the world; I remain.
Every test life gave me, from exams to heartbreaks, I faced with the sense that my real self was like a pure thing rubbed on a touchstone, always passing.
Write a doha about the Self, which is like pure metal that the touchstone rubs without leaving any mark, unalterable, unbreakable, and always itself no matter how it is tested by life.
doha on the temple with the true self inside us
temple, the real dweller
Write a verse about the temple of this life where the dweller within has never been created, never carved, and never installed, for the Self is unborn and always there.
Inside the old temple I felt that the quiet in me was older than every carving in the place and would outlast them all.
Stones are carved for the temple and the god is said to dwell there, but the dweller was never built and never brought in.
A diamond may be locked in a vault, a door may be barred, but the Self is never behind any door.
door, diamond, deathless self
Compose a verse about the Self within that cannot be shut behind a door and that is more precious than any diamond, because it is beyond price, beyond loss, and has no beginning.
Every time I locked my diamond ring in the drawer I realized how little the things I protect resemble the one who protects them.
the soul is the door and the diamond, can i get a doha about it
Write a verse on the peacock dancing in its brilliant colours and the seed asleep in the soil, both carrying the same deathless Self which does not begin with the form and does not end with it.
peacock, seed, one Self
doha about the peacock and the seed and what stays
The peacock dances in the monsoon, yet the dancer within the dance is unborn, and every seed holds that same dancer.
I watched a peacock dance in the field where my father had planted a single seed, and I felt the same invisible presence in both of them.
Seeing a forgotten cloth sheet at the crossroads, I thought the one who wore it, and indeed every one of us, is more than any covering.
At the crossroads, a cloth sheet lies in the dust; the wearer has moved on, unharmed.
crossroads, cloth sheet, soul

Write a doha about the cloth sheet spread at the crossroads that the Self has no need of, since the Self was never cold, never covered, and never born, and does not need protection from anything at all.
doha on crossroads and a cloth sheet but about the soul
needle, the unpierced Self
When the doctor's needle went into my arm I strangely felt that whoever was feeling it was not harmed at all.
doha on the soul and the needle
A needle may pierce the cloth but never the one who wears it; the Self cannot be wounded.
Compose a doha about the Self which no needle can pierce, no knot can bind, and no craft can mend, for it is whole in itself and has never been torn or sewn.
doha on the soul that doesn't come or go
My friend said at his father's funeral that his father was not gone, he simply was not in sight, and I found myself believing him.
Write a verse about the Self which never arrives and never departs, which remains where it always was while forms come and go around it.
no birth, no death
Not born in the dark, not buried in the day, the quiet one within is neither coming nor going.
I saw a crow pecking near the old man's shroud and felt, sharply, that the person we all knew had never been in that thing.
shroud, crow, what lives on
doha about the soul when the shroud and the crow come
Write a doha about the shroud and the crow that wait at the end of every body, and the quiet Self that has already left both behind, never to be touched by cloth or by claw.
The shroud is wound around the form and the crow waits near; but the one who lived in it is far beyond.
In the middle of a panic attack I noticed that something in me was calmly watching the panic, and that something seemed untouchable.
Deeper than thought, older than memory, the watcher sits awake while the whole dream passes by.
whats the thing in me that watches my thoughts? doha
the inner witness
Write me a verse about the silent presence that watches every thought, every emotion, and every day pass, which is never itself a thought, an emotion, or a day but the one who is aware of all.
Waves rise and fall, the ocean stays; so lives the Self beneath the rise and fall of lives.
Standing by the ocean on my father's birthday, I felt that the wave of him had gone but the water he was made of was right here.
ocean, the endless Self
Compose a verse about the endless ocean of the Self in which every individual life is only a wave that rises, shines for a moment, and returns, while the water itself is never born and never lost.
doha: soul is like the ocean, never ending
The river passes through the towns and carries none of them; so does the Self pass through its lives.
doha about the river that is the soul, flowing on
Write a doha on how a river keeps flowing through all the places it passes without ever being those places, as the deathless Self passes through all of life's stages without being any of them.
river, ever-flowing Self
Walking beside the river at dusk, I felt there was a constant in me that had moved through childhood, youth, and now middle age without being touched by any of them.
A hunter's arrow once passed through the branch where a cuckoo was singing, and the song went on, as if the singer was never in the branch.
The cuckoo's call is only the arrow of sound, but the one who calls and the one who hears is the same unborn Self.
Write a verse on the arrow that hurts the form and the cuckoo that sings from it, with the unborn Self beyond both, untouched by the arrow's wound and the cuckoo's song alike.
doha on the arrow and the cuckoo and the soul
arrow, cuckoo, one Self
the swan and the oil press: doha on the soul
Write a verse about the swan gliding on the water, not wet, not touched, and the oil press that grinds seeds all day, and let both show how the Self remains pure while the world is crushed around it.
The swan glides without wetting its wings, and the press grinds on; the Self is a swan in all the world's grinding.
swan, oil press, pure Self
Through months of grinding work at the oil press, my uncle floated through like a swan, as if he were someone else watching the work.
ageless, unborn
At my grandmother's ninetieth birthday she laughed like a girl and said that inside she was still exactly sixteen and always had been.
who is it that never grows old in me? doha
Write a verse about the part of me that was the same when I was five and will be the same when I am eighty, which has never grown old and does not recognise itself as having any age.
The years write on the face but not on the writer, who sits behind the eyes forever young.
untouched by joy, sorrow
Give me a verse about the Self within that is beyond happiness and sadness, that neither gains from success nor loses from failure, and watches the whole play of life like an unmoved spectator.
Beyond the pairs of joy and sorrow, beyond the gain and loss, lives one who was never touched by either.
doha on the self that isn't moved by joy or pain
After the wedding and the funeral in the same week, I felt that the one who observed both days stayed perfectly even.
doha on a lock and a fly, but about the soul
Compose a verse about the Self within that no lock can hold and no fly can disturb, for the Self is always free, beyond every bar and every pest of the passing world.
Locked in a waiting room for hours with a fly buzzing, I felt a freedom in me that no lock could ever have kept.
No lock holds the one who is everywhere, and the fly that buzzes at the window is not even noticed by the sky within.
lock, fly, the free Self
soul vs ego, who am i, doha pls
In the middle of my busiest week, I paused and wondered about who was actually doing all these things, and for a moment I felt perfectly empty and perfectly full.
Not the doer but the ground of doing, not the sound but the silence from which all sound arises, and to which it returns.
the ground of being
Write a doha about the soul as the one who is not the thinker of thoughts, nor the doer of deeds, nor the sufferer of pains, but the ground on which all of those appear and disappear.
While watching the crowd at the railway station I felt that every stranger in it carried the same quiet presence behind the eyes.
One Self in a thousand faces, one breath in a thousand lives, one dreamer in a thousand dreams.
Please give me a verse about the one Self shining in all people alike, in the rich and in the poor, in the wise and in the foolish, undivided, untouched, and equal everywhere.
one Self in all
something about the soul being the same in everyone
It cannot be harmed, ended, worn down, or lessened; it was before the world, and it will be after.
indestructible Self
After surviving the accident that should have killed me, I felt as if some part of me had been entirely unreachable the whole time.
doha on the soul that nothing can destroy
Write a verse on the Self that nothing can wound, that no force can diminish, that no loss can touch, because it was never made of anything that can be harmed.
A drop in the ocean is the ocean in a drop; the Self within me is the Self within all.
doha on the ocean and the soul being a drop
ocean, drop, same Self
Write a doha about the drop that thinks itself separate until it falls into the ocean and finds that it was always the ocean, just as the individual self finds it was always the whole.
Floating in the ocean for the first time, I felt my edges soften and I wondered if the separate me was only a story.
seed, the unborn
doha about the seed that never really dies
The tiny seed holds the whole wood, the wood holds the seed; the Self is unborn, yet becomes all the forms.
Write a verse about the seed that seems to die in the soil and rise again as a plant, as the unborn Self seems to vanish and reappear but is never created or destroyed.
In the garden I buried a seed and told my daughter that it wasn't dying but changing form, and then I felt I was saying it about us.
My friend stayed tied to his past by the thinnest rope of habit, and I told him that the real him had never been held by it.
The rope binds the hand, not the one who holds it; the Self was free before the first knot.
doha on the self being free of any rope
rope, the unbound Self
Compose a doha about the soul that has never been tied by any rope, never bound by any chain, and that only imagines itself captured, like a person who fears a harm that is not there.
Write a doha on the Self that walks through thorns at every crossroads of life, bleeding in appearance only, because the one who walks is not the one who is pricked and remains whole.
thorn, crossroads, steady Self
Thorns line the crossroads and the feet may bleed, but the walker within is whole, unpierced, unbowed.
doha about the soul among thorns at the crossroads
After my third heartbreak, standing at a crossroads with my feet full of thorns from the jungle trail, I felt a part of me was entirely unhurt.
Watching the washerman at the riverbank scrub my father's old clothes, I felt that the owner of those clothes was not even a little bit in them.
doha about the washerman and the real me
washerman, spotless Self
The washerman beats the cloth at the bank; the one who wears it was never soiled.
Write a verse about how the washerman scrubs the cloth until it shines, and no washing can make the Self clean or dirty, for it was always spotless and has never been stained.
